angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 497,426 km at 118.92 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.4088 +/- 0.0113 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 118.92 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.715 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Veldhuis et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1259 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.272V/abstract): 497,426 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.746 +/- 0.048 solar masses from Veldhuis et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1259 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.272V/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4775 +/- 100 K from Martin et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of TOI-1259 A b's parameter set from Martin et al. 2021 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.4132M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Martin et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of TOI-1259 A b's parameter set from Martin et al. 2021 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.4132M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1259-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.602, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
